claim: In 1878 Western Union's electrician describes the telegraph spring-jack: a spring strip with a brass pin pressed against another pin; pressing a wedge carrying the instrument wires between the pins breaks the main-line circuit. 'This device is termed a spring-jack.'

When the wedge carrying the instrument wires is pressed in between the two pins it separates them

notes: A WEDGE, not a round plug. Locator p. 451 is the scout's reading of the book's page.
